title: Kingdom of Janggala
capsule: The Kingdom of Janggala was one of two Javanese successor states created when the aging king Airlangga abdicated around 1045–1046 and divided his realm to avoid civil war between rival sons, with Janggala occupying the northeastern portion of East Java (roughly the Brantas delta and Malang highlands) and Panjalu (Kediri) the western portion. Janggala is the less-documented of the two kingdoms; it appears in Old Javanese inscriptions and the kakawin literature as a distinct political entity maintaining its own court and administrative structure. The kingdom was absorbed by the expanding Kediri kingdom around the mid-twelfth century, and its territory was later incorporated into Singhasari and ultimately the Majapahit empire.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The territorial extent of Janggala is poorly attested; its boundaries are inferred from a small number of inscriptions and retrospective literary sources rather than contemporary administrative records, and the precise division from Kediri is debated.
